4. AIA – Resilient Performance and More Sustainable Growth

- AIA's share price has held up much better vs. China's domestic names over the past 2-3 months, as the company has seen very limited impact from market volatility; 1Q26 disclosed VNB data only, with no earnings.

- VNB growth is still key for investors to track; we think China could be the engine, helping it maintain ~15% VNB growth in FY26 and FY27, and 13% growth in 1Q is on-track with full-year consensus growth.
- Buybacks could support the share price in 2Q26. However, we see limited near-term catalysts.
- Valuation at 1.35x 26E P/EV is higher than peers, with 12-month VNB multiple of 3.7x; we see FY26E EV growth at >10%.
AIA has completed HKD6.2bn buyback as of May 14, ~US$0.8bn vs. planned US$1.7bn

4. Ping An – Strong High-Quality Growth and Less Property Drag
- Ping An's share price underwent some correction, mainly dragged by China peers amid the 4Q25 slowdown, concerns over 1Q26 earnings, weak market sentiment, and national team selling.

- However, 1Q26 results were solid, and management expects AM to become profit-making in 2026 – one year earlier than previous market expectation, suggesting the property drag could finally come to an end.
• We think growth in 2026 could be healthy and of higher quality, with the CSM balance returning to positive growth.
- FY26E P/B is 0.90x and dividend yield has returned to ~5.3%, which we view as more appealing.

4. China Life – Leading VNB Growth in 2026 and Potential for Further Valuation Upside
- China Life's H-share price saw a sharper correction before end-April, due to a mix of factors including market rumors, weak stock market performance, and volatile earnings in 4Q25 and 1Q26.
• However, the 1Q26 results overhang appears to be fully factored in, and we expect potentially stronger 2Q earnings considering the market rebound. Its VNB growth in 1Q26 was at a strong 76%.
• FY26E P/B is 1.1x, higher than key peers, though investors may be willing to pay a premium in a bull market.
- Longer-term P&L volatility is still a key concern for LO investors.

4. PICC P&C – CoR Improvement Potential amid Deregulation
- PICC P&C's share price has also been weak since end-2025 and was not defensive amid market uncertainty.
- Management has set clear 2026 guidance: auto CoR no worse than FY25's \(95.3\%\) and non-auto CoR \(< 100\%\).
• We still see some short-term uncertainties, including 1) a high CoR base in 1H25; 2) limited cat losses in 2025; and 3) slow premium growth in 1Q26.
- However, FY26E P/B is currently 0.95x and dividend yield is appealing at ~5.6%, both of which we see as attractive, especially for LO investors.

4. CPIC – More Appealing Valuation, but We Need to See More Catalysts
- CPIC has underperformed peers since late 2025, with lower market interest due to both liability-side concerns in 1H25 and asset-side concerns in 3Q25.

- Its 1Q26 earnings outperformed most peers with positive net profit growth. The agency channel continues to improve quality, while the banca channel focuses on structure optimization and compliant operations.
• Valuation is more appealing at P/B of 0.83x, lower than its key peers.
• However, we expect VNB growth to be lower than peers, with a lack of short-term catalysts.
